ownPresentation.label: Char enumFromTo
ownPresentation.description: The `Enumerable Char` step: the bounded codepoint range [lo..hi] inclusive as a pure cons-spine `List Char`, stepping by the next Unicode codepoint. charEnumFromTo lo hi = if gt (charCode lo) (charCode hi) then Nil else Cons lo (charEnumFromTo (charFromCode (add (charCode lo) 1)) hi). Composes the host leaves charCode/charFromCode (NO new leaf); the order is by codepoint (charCode), exactly as charLt orders Chars. lo > hi (by codepoint) ⇒ Nil; lo == hi ⇒ singleton. Total over the bounded range (recurses on the shrinking codepoint gap; the totality checker returns Unknown — the intEnumFromTo precedent).

ownPresentation.label: Document from HTML
ownPresentation.description: Import the bounded lowercase XHTML-style fragment emitted by Document as HTML into the same typed Document. Accept paragraphs, composed emphasis/strong, code, safe links, nested sections and document-note asides, with the five XML entities and decimal/hex scalar references decoded once. Preserve text whitespace and explicit empty elements; CR and attribute TAB/LF/CR require numeric references to avoid XML normalization. Merge adjacent text nodes and remove empty text nodes. Unknown syntax, attributes, unsafe links, invalid characters, multiline headings, source over 8192 code points or traversal over 64 steps returns Err with a code-point location. This is not a general HTML/XML parser or a Markdown round-trip claim.

ownPresentation.label: Document from Markdown
ownPresentation.description: Import a bounded Markdown/XHTML fragment into the same typed Document: blank-line-separated single-line paragraphs, consecutive-level ATX headings, backtick code spans/fences, composed XHTML emphasis/strong and safe links, empty inline-code fallbacks, and exact XHTML paragraph/code/note blocks terminated by a blank line or EOF. Standard outlines attach following blocks to the latest heading; explicit section ends are not recoverable. Merge adjacent text, remove empty text, decode bounded XML entities once outside literal code, and ignore exact backtick-separator comments. Delimiter emphasis, bracket links/images, lists, quotes, soft wraps, paragraph/opening indentation, general HTML, unsafe links, malformed syntax, literal CR, source over 8192 code points and normalized export-depth failures return Err with a code-point location. Round trips apply to outline-shaped representable Documents within both bounds, not arbitrary original trees or all CommonMark.

ownPresentation.label: Int enumFromTo
ownPresentation.description: The `Enumerable Int` step: the bounded integer range [lo..hi] inclusive as a pure cons-spine `List Int`. intEnumFromTo lo hi = if intLt hi lo then Nil else Cons lo (intEnumFromTo (intAdd lo (numberToInt 1)) hi). The step unit is built via numberToInt 1 (the bridge path, not a Succ-literal — the numeric-tower §0.2 stack hazard); intAdd/intLt compose the Phase-2 Int bodies. lo > hi ⇒ Nil (empty range); lo == hi ⇒ a singleton. Total over the bounded-interval domain (recurses on the shrinking hi − lo measure; the totality checker returns Unknown — the natDiv precedent).

ownPresentation.label: Number to Int
ownPresentation.description: Materialize a whole Number as a sign-magnitude Int: mkInt (numberToNat (abs n)) (lt n 0). The magnitude is the Peano materialization of |n|; the sign is (n < 0). numberToInt 0 ⇒ +0 (abs 0 = 0 ⇒ Zero magnitude ⇒ mkInt forces negative = False), so the bridge never emits −0. Defined over the ℤ domain (fractional parts floor-clamp through numberToNat).

ownPresentation.label: Number to Nat
ownPresentation.description: Materialize a non-negative whole Number as a Peano Nat (Succ^n Zero). numberToNat n = if n <= 0 then Zero else Succ (numberToNat (n - 1)). For n <= 0 (and the fractional part of any non-integer) it returns the floor-clamped-to-Zero Peano value — the bridge is defined over the Nat domain [0,∞). Terminates by the guarded Number decrement (below the totality checker's Nat rungs ⇒ Unknown; total over the intended ℕ domain).

ownPresentation.label: Orderable pair
ownPresentation.description: True iff the ordering leaf can compare these two values: both numbers, or both strings. Every other pairing — mixed number/string, two booleans, two records, two lists — is NOT orderable, and `minimum`/`maximum` fence to Nothing rather than guess. ownPresentation.label: Combined error bound 2/(k+1)
ownPresentation.description: The combined-error Rational 2/(k+1) at precision k = mkRational 2 (k+1), built via the NUMBER BRIDGES (numberToInt over add (natToNumber k) 1) rather than Succ-literals. WHY THE BRIDGE PATH: feeding a Succ-literal-built or mkInt-built Nat/Int (e.g. `mkInt (Succ k) False`) into mkRational — which runs natGcd/natDiv on it — triggers an engine evaluation blow-up (Maximum-call-stack; see the roadmap Phase-4 surprises), whereas numberToInt/numberToNat-built values feed the deep arithmetic recursion cleanly. So eps2 routes k through the bridge (Nat → Number → Int) — robust + still exact for the small k a fuel-bounded search reaches. The Real comparison separation test declares two reals separated when their sampled approximations differ by more than this. Decreases toward 0 linearly (the 1/(k+1) modulus convention).

ownPresentation.label: Real equal (partial)
ownPresentation.description: realEq a b fuel : Maybe Bool — equality with an explicit Nat fuel budget. Equality is NEVER positively confirmable by finite sampling (the sequences could agree arbitrarily long then diverge), so this is SOUND-conservative: if a and b SEPARATE within budget (realSeparate returns Just _, either direction), they are unequal ⇒ Just False; otherwise ⇒ Nothing (cannot confirm equality). It NEVER returns Just True — the degenerate definitional Just-True (syntactic identity) is omitted as a deliberate soundness choice (never a Just we cannot witness). Nothing IS the decidability boundary as a value (D4/north-star §6).

ownPresentation.label: Real separate

At each precision k take sepDecision (realSampleAt a k) (realSampleAt b k) (ratEps2 k): a Just is a witness (Just True = a<b, Just False = a>b) returned immediately; a Nothing means the samples still overlap, so increase precision (Succ k), consume one fuel, and retry. Recurses STRUCTURALLY on fuel ⇒ total (the partiality is in the Maybe codomain, not termination).

ownPresentation.description: Three numbers, sorted, then reversed. Open it to see the steps as a graph and as code.

People, projects and a mascot are ordinary typed data. Rom is Fenel's author; Aajonus is the Primal Diet's, whose two formulas are references to recipe functions; Healthfully, by Bayne and Rom, names the Primal Diet as its inspiration. Fenel is named after common fennel, takes giant fennel as its emblem, is inspired by ten programming languages, and its logo by the fennels. Edit in Local copies them into Local with the plants, their genera and family; open a project's dependencies to follow the links. A change to a person or a plant updates everything that references it. Unconfirmed personal details and social links stay absent.

Two recipes, each a pure function: the moisturizing-lubrication formula and the sports formula. Each takes the foods you have and returns every preparation it allows with them. Open one to see its expression and the facts derived from it. Examples gives the moisturizing-lubrication formula three lists of foods: one preparation comes out, then two, then none. Edit in Local copies the moisturizing-lubrication formula, the foods it chooses from and its facts into Local; change the function or turn foods off and on to recompute its facts. The examples make no health claim.

Call solve on an ordinary predicate function and a domain: exact answers to linear systems, every answer in a finite domain, train routes and meeting slots over typed rows, and honest Unknown answers. Change typed inputs and inspect the evidence.
All life, then kingdoms, classes, families and species, with the pictures we made. Each set is judged inside the one above it by Fenel's set judgment; foods name the living thing they come from.

A plant family is the set of its species, and each genus a subset of it; the sets by life form cut across the families. The fennels are a set made by people, not by botany: common fennel and giant fennel, whose smallest common botanical group also holds carrot. Fenel's set judgment decides each subset, disjointness, union and intersection on the species records. The sets hold the species described in this collection; other species are not listed.
Browse the existing country data, filter by currency and use the matching country codes as a generated input type. Changes stay local.
Browse the modern Greek alphabet, combine letter sets and try bounded unaccented text against the same selected characters.

More alphabets beside the Greek one: the 26 Latin letters, the 33 letters of the Russian alphabet with a Latin transliteration, the 24 runes of the Elder Futhark with their reconstructed names, and the 46 basic hiragana and katakana with their Hepburn readings. Each mark comes first, its reading in the corner.
Ten programming languages Fenel learns from, each with the year it first appeared and what Fenel takes from it. Fenel's project record points at this list.
Correct typed inputs, compare fixed password rules and check whole credentials or nested orders through the same membership judgment.
Edit a function of x, inspect its typed points and path, then compose circles, lines and a filled polygon into an image.
Earlier demos that have not been reworked yet. They may be rough.
Open the contact input type, change its temporary draft and fill in the generated input beside it. Reset restores the example.

Edit a small encoded image as ordinary rows of RGBA pixel data, explore the supplied market photograph and a photo expression with rotation, colour inversion, blur and a layered landscape, then explore the original landscape and composed raster filters. Color frequencies and spectra retain separate source data.
Choose a reader language while the multilingual data and source stay unchanged.
Edit numbers or customer purchases, then inspect Fenel-computed summaries, grouped totals and a chart of the original numbers.

Inspect named regex groups or bounded Lisp trees, decode retained UTF-8 files, format JSON, or convert CSV text tables and JSON records while preserving every cell as text. The declared purchase format adds checked purchases and customer totals. Invalid input keeps its errors.
Move the Drawing scene with a Fenel time formula, play a bounded frame sequence, and inspect exact snapshots.

Catalogue-based planning: choose ingredients, personal exclusions and preparation time, then inspect which catalogue recipes qualify and each rule's reasons. The separate Recipe functions example edits functions and derives criteria from their bodies.

Author a typed document, derive its outline and email draft, export Markdown or XHTML-compatible HTML, and read bounded XHTML or Markdown back into editable data. Markdown headings form an outline. Unsupported input returns an error.
Inspect a claim's definition, finite domain, exact kernel verdict or sample evidence. Concrete counterexamples and undecided answers retain their own grades.
Explore seven families of Fenel's foundations through ordinary data and editable examples. Assumed foundations, concrete checks and undecided answers keep their own meaning.

value.meaning: Common fennel and giant fennel: the species of this collection that people call fennel. No family or genus holds just these two. NCBI Taxonomy places common fennel (filed there as Anethum foeniculum) in tribe Apieae, with dill and celery, and Ferula in tribe Scandiceae, with carrot. The smallest botanical group holding both is subfamily Apioideae, which also holds carrot, celery, coriander and dill.
